repo_notes.content: Describe Misty as the browser workspace in the current README.md: tabs, split panes, bookmarks, agents, and encrypted cross-device workspace sync, with Spaces for collaborative work. Cover the complete repository: the React frontend in src/, the Tauri/Rust host and workers in src-tauri/, the Go backend and TypeScript services in server/, and the Rust development/release CLI in cli/. Desktop development and sync currently target macOS and Windows; a separate web build has different capabilities. Mobile and tablet shells and build targets have been removed. Derive platform support from active entrypoints and platform gates rather than unused dependencies or historical plans.

Use the indexed branch's executable source, route registration, manifests, migrations, and tests as the authority. README.md, feature READMEs, DESIGN.md files, and docs/ provide context but can contain superseded checkpoints. Resolve contradictions by tracing current callers. State the difference between implemented behavior, automated test coverage, live platform verification, and remaining work. Cite source files for substantive claims and show end-to-end data flows across the frontend, native host, and server where relevant. Do not infer production deployment or universal browser-session compatibility from code or fixture tests.

Prioritize the browser/device sync architecture, desktop companion, account isolation, current Scheduled tasks, settings profiles, and the consolidated server and CLI. Keep distinct the encrypted browser vault/tree protocol, settings-profile synchronization, Space collaboration, and peer file transport: they have different state owners, transports, permissions, and persistence. Also distinguish bookmarks using legacy group/website wire records from visible tab groups and saved tab groups; verify which metadata actually syncs rather than promising cross-device tab-group parity.

Retired installable apps/SDK, Activepieces workflows, the old user-routine scheduler, waitlist systems, and mobile targets are historical context, not current product architecture. Built-in tools compile with Misty; native workers are bundled with the desktop build. The current src/features/scheduled/ and server scheduled-task handlers are active and must be documented separately from retired routines. Migration archives and compatibility routes do not imply that a retired subsystem is available. Use .config/retired-repository-history.json and current runtime composition to explain relevant transitions briefly.

Prefer reproducible setup and command examples from package.json, cli/README.md, cli/src/, .config/tooling.json, and server/README.md. Separate Vite-only frontend development from the signed native Tauri launcher, and separate starting containers from explicitly deploying collaboration Workers. Explain isolated desktop development profiles for two-device testing. Verify environment variable names against their owning configuration code; document their role and required/optional status without copying secrets or local environment values. Do not resurrect removed npm mobile commands.

Document important trust boundaries as part of the architecture: renderer versus native secrets and browser data, account/deployment isolation, Space membership, authenticated device grants, run-scoped MCP authorization, tool approvals, and companion screen/input permissions. Explain teardown on logout, account switching, lock, cancellation, and loss of ownership where implemented. Show actual enforcement paths and failure behavior rather than asserting blanket security or platform guarantees.

The public Go repository contains product services and an optional billing adapter; commercial billing policy lives in a separate private repository. The website and user documentation may live in misty-website or the GitHub wiki, outside this checkout. Explain those integration boundaries without inventing their internals. vendor/clicky is reference source for the companion, and src-tauri/vendor contains native dependency patches. Personal .agents/, .claude/, .codex/, and .impeccable/ directories are optional local tooling, not Misty runtime components or required build dependencies.

Use the explicit page hierarchy below as the full documentation plan. Keep overview pages concise and link to the detailed pages instead of repeating them. Source paths in page notes are starting points, not exhaustive file lists: follow their active imports, registered handlers, storage adapters, and relevant tests. Avoid copying hard-coded feature limits, dependency versions, test counts, deployment hostnames, or readiness claims from old prose; derive them from the indexed implementation and configuration.
